$comment: IOS-MOVE-ME (R1270, R1271, R204). The /api/v1/me codec, before and after it moved from org.json in :app to :shared commonMain (kotlinx.serialization). `answers[].old` and `patches[].oldBody` are what the OLD codec RETURNED, captured by running it at 7df4d9fa (the JVM org.json library in :app's tests) before it was deleted - never typed. android/shared/src/commonTest/kotlin/ch/monreleve/app/settings/MeCodecGoldenTest.kt requires the moved codec to return the same (on the JVM and on the iOS simulator); android/app/src/test/kotlin/ch/monreleve/app/startup/MeRouteJoinTest.kt requires RESOLVING to decide `old.start` on every body and the app to send every patch `body` exactly; web/tests/db/me-cases-join.test.ts seeds each answer `row` and requires the REAL GET route to answer that `body` byte for byte, and PATCHes every patch `body` to the REAL route. A case's `divergence` is where the new codec differs from the old, with the new result and why; the golden asserts the set by name. A patch `body` is the old code's put() order (Android's org.json kept insertion order); `oldBody` is the JVM library's HashMap order, so the two are compared as JSON values, not bytes.

divergence.why: The JVM org.json library refuses a body that repeats a key; kotlinx.serialization keeps the LAST value (measured, run 1). The route never repeats a key (it writes one object through JSON.stringify), so no answer the server gives is affected. Android's own org.json was not run (it is stubbed under JVM tests).

The JVM org.json library read the first object and ignored the text after it; kotlinx.serialization parses STRICT JSON and refuses the whole body, so it reads as not a /me answer (Unresolved, a retry), never as an account. The route never writes text after its object.

answers.name: a second object after the first

divergence.why: As for trailing text: the JVM org.json library read the first object only; kotlinx.serialization refuses the body (Unresolved, a retry). The route writes one object.

The JVM org.json library is lenient and read unquoted keys and single-quoted strings; kotlinx.serialization (wireJson, isLenient = false) refuses them (Unresolved, a retry). The route writes strict JSON.
The JVM org.json library accepted a comma before the closing brace; kotlinx.serialization refuses it (Unresolved, a retry). The route writes strict JSON.
